newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mediterranean officials meet in Algiers on energy.
newsitem.headline: Mediterranean officials meet in Algiers on energy.

text.p: Mediterranean energy groups officials on Saturday met in Algiers to discuss cooperation in power projects, said the Algerian official news agency APS.

"They discussed the creation of a joint firm specialised in electricity production and ways of financing a power project in southern Algeria," said APS quoting Nazim Zouioueche, head of the Algerian state-owned oil and gas firm Sonatrach.

The Mediterranean officials, taking part in Algiers's Energy Mediterranean Observatory (EMO) gathering, are representative of French oil company Total and electricity Edf firm, Italy energy group Eni, Endsa group and Red Electrica from Spain and Sonatrach from Algeria.

Four newly admitted EMO's energy companies, Societe electrique of Lebanon, French Elf-Aquitaine group, Adison from Italy and Transgas from Portugal respresentatives also attended the meeting, APS said.
Officials from British Petroleum corporation, which was admitted as an associated member in the observatory, took part in the energy gathering, it added.
The EMO was set up in 1991 by energy independent firms in the aim of boosting energy cooperation in both shores of the Mediterranean sea.
The EMO members held talks in the Italian Trieste city in last June over gas cooperation.
